name: Bowling Green State University
academic_ranking: Bowling Green State University is a public research university (Carnegie R2) in northwest Ohio enrolling roughly 18,000-19,000 students. It is well regarded for programs in education, business (Schmidthorst College of Business), psychology, and the health sciences, and is recognized for undergraduate teaching and student success/retention efforts.
financial_aid: Public university offering in-state and out-of-state rates under the Falcon Tuition Guarantee (a fixed four-year rate locked by entering cohort). Non-resident tuition equals the instructional fee plus an out-of-state surcharge. Merit- and need-based aid, scholarships, grants, and work-study are available through the BGSU Office of Student Financial Aid; athletic scholarships for softball are administered per NCAA Division I limits. Exact current-year figures published via the BGSU Bursar tuition-and-fees page.
facilities_notes: Softball competes at the BGSU Softball Field on the Bowling Green campus. Falcon athletics facilities include the Sebo Athletic Center (strength/conditioning and support services) and the Stroh Center; team support includes athletic training staff shared with other programs.
program_reputation: Bowling Green softball competes in NCAA Division I in the Mid-American Conference. Head coach Michelle Gardner, hired to lead the program, brings extensive Division I experience including head-coaching stints at Nevada and Indiana and a College World Series appearance as an assistant at Arizona State, plus associate head coach experience at Coastal Carolina. She also began her coaching career at BGSU in 1992.
